prime_age_share.label: Residents in their prime working years (ages 25 to 54)
prime_age_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program (Vintage 2025)
prime_age_share.note: Share of all residents who are 25 to 54, the ages when most people work. Modeled estimates; each new vintage revises back to 2020.

age65_share.label: Residents 65 and older
age65_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program (Vintage 2025)
age65_share.note: Share of all residents who are 65 or older. Modeled estimates; each new vintage revises back to 2020.

prime_age_epop.label: Prime-age workers: share of people 25 to 54 with a job
prime_age_epop.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B23001
prime_age_epop.note: People 25 to 54 who are employed (civilian jobs plus armed forces) as a share of all people 25 to 54, including those in group quarters. Counties where 5% or more of residents live in group quarters (prisons, college dorms, nursing homes) are flagged, because those residents rarely hold jobs. Survey estimate; ± is the 90% margin of error by the Census approximation for proportions.

general_fertility_rate.label: Fertility rate: births per 1,000 women ages 15 to 44
general_fertility_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program (Vintage 2025): births and women 15 to 44
general_fertility_rate.note: The general fertility rate: births in the year ending June 30, per 1,000 women ages 15 to 44 (average of the July 1 estimates at the start and end of the year). Births come from National Center for Health Statistics records; the latest year is partly estimated and is revised in the next vintage. CDC's births-per-woman measure is not published for small counties.
